summary: A shadow-only signed-tree job reports whether a pull request would be rejected for lacking a trusted signed note; nothing is required or rejected

schema.detail: No daemon claim or portable record change.

rules.detail: A new workflow (Signed tree (shadow), pull_request_target, run from the base branch) runs scripts/ci-signed-tree on same-repository non-draft pull requests and prints what scripts/evidence-verify --require-all would decide for the head tree; the skip policy marks genie-freshness and typescript-client require:shadow. The job always passes, is not a required check, reads no secret, checks out and runs no pull request code, and no enforce changes, so no job is skipped or rejected.

compatibility.detail: One extra light job (ubuntu-latest, a few seconds to about a minute) per pull request event; no existing check or workflow changes.

recovery.detail: Reverting removes the workflow and the require markers; no state is written.
